window: I've tried to do the block-based thing with AF networking, and I prefer that to delegates. But I feel like if you did that in a controller, it's deodorant for the fact that your controller is trying to do too much stuff. If you need your controller to have more than one or two delegates on it, then probably that's the universe telling you that maybe your controller's trying to do too many things, and you should kind of be pulling that out into separate little helper classes. Mm-hmm.

I get a little bit frustrated trying to do things with blocks because I think because I have happy experiences doing that in JavaScript land and it's really easy to just create anonymous functions. And in Objective-C, it's quite painful to do stuff with blocks. It's better than not having blocks, but it's still not as easy as in some other languages. So I always get quite frustrated trying to do stuff with blocks because it feels like it should be super easy. And then I end up having to...
remember what stuff has to be retained in the weak duty dude and under under block and all that stuff and i just get annoyed and throw my hands up in you yep that's pretty common

I do a pretty common example in this networking presentation that I've been giving. And I take the new NSURL session block-based handler for an image download. And then once I get it working, it's kind of like download tasks with a URL. And then it takes a block, one single block, which gives you the URL of the downloaded file, whether or not there was an error and the task itself or the response.

And then I say, okay, now I want to show progress for this download. And unfortunately, progress is not supported using that block-based form. So I have to sort of convert it back into the NSURL session delegates methods. And what happens is interesting that you have, say, one block that is handling the callback for this request. And inside the block, you need to do a bunch of things like

disable the network activity indicator spinner, and you need to check to see if there's an error, and if so, you probably need to throw some sort of alert or update the user interface in some way, which requires dispatching onto the main thread, the main queue. Then you check the response. If there's no error, then you actually got a response, so then you have to cast the URL response to an HTTP response.

to get the status code. Then you check that to see if it's 200. If it's not 200, again, you're updating user interface with some sort of alert that has to be dispatched on the main queue. And then if you did get a 200, then you need to copy the file somewhere else. And in my case, I was doing it on a, just to a UI image in memory and then jump onto the main queue to set that onto the image view. So you can imagine what kind of a indentation nightmare that, you know, three different if branches and there's a bunch of dispatching happening and there's the disabling of the network activity indicator. All of those

sifted into a much tinier method when done in the delegate variant. There's one callback that tells you when the request finished, and that's the place where you would get the error. And there's another one that tells you whether or not the file was downloaded, so all the file download transfer stuff goes there. It just cleaned everything up and put all those things into a distinct method, which is like your next refactoring trick in your pocket that you would take. You have this nasty-looking block method that

Now let me shift this into other methods. So, I don't know, like, blocks are awesome, but I think that sometimes they get overused. When there are too many parameters, sometimes it's just nicer to already have those methods predefined and each thing has its place. Yeah, that sounds good. Just make everything explicit, clean, and a bit hard to test. Ciao.

Any other tricks you guys want to share before we wrap this up? It's good stuff. I think the main thing that we've kind of said in various different ways is that MVC is a really nice pattern and it's really well implemented in iOS, but it doesn't mean everything has to be an M of E or a C. Então vamos à causa de tudo isso, que é a guerra no Oriente Médio. O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, deu um novo ultimato ao Irã e afirmou que o país pode ser eliminado até a noite desta terça-feira. A declaração foi dada durante uma coletiva na Casa Branca na tarde desta segunda e é uma tentativa de forçar o Irã a reabrir o Estreito de Hormuz.
O prazo é nove da noite dessa terça-feira, no horário de Brasília. Trump prometeu destruir a infraestrutura básica do país, como pontes e centrais elétricas, caso não haja rendição.

Temos um plano, por causa do poder do nosso exército, em que todas as pontos do Irã serão dizimadas até meia-noite de amanhã, onde todas as usinas do Irã estarão fora do mercado, queimando, explodindo e nunca mais serão usadas. Quero dizer, demolição completa vai acontecer em um período de quatro horas, se quisermos. Não queremos que isso aconteça.

O presidente ainda sugeriu que os Estados Unidos podem passar a cobrar um pedágio para quem navegar pelo Estreito de Hormuz, mas ele não explicou como faria essa cobrança. O governo do Irã rejeitou qualquer acordo que não garanta o fim definitivo dos ataques dos Estados Unidos e de Israel. O vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores do Irã, Kazem Garibabad, afirmou nas redes sociais que Donald Trump está ameaçando cometer crimes de guerra e violar o direito internacional.

Aliados dos Estados Unidos e especialistas também criticaram a postura da Casa Branca, alertando para as consequências humanitárias de um ataque total contra o Irã. Antes dessa fala do presidente Trump, a guarda revolucionária do Irã tinha dito numa rede social que o Estreito de Hormuz nunca mais voltará ao seu estado anterior, especialmente para os Estados Unidos e Israel.

E os governos americano e do Irã também rejeitaram nesta segunda-feira uma proposta de cessar fogo elaborada pelo Paquistão para tentar encerrar o conflito. Esse plano, batizado de Acordo de Islamabad, previa duas fases. Uma trégua imediata de 45 dias com a reabertura do Estreito de Hormuz, seguida de negociações para um pacto definitivo.

O presidente Trump confirmou o recebimento do texto, mas disse que os termos ainda não são suficientes. Ele também baixou ainda mais o nível ao responder sobre o cometimento de crimes de guerra, dizendo que não está preocupado sobre os alertas por alvejar infraestrutura civil, porque, segundo ele, os iranianos são animais. Ele disse que o crime de guerra é permitir que o Irã tenha uma arma nuclear.

E eu aproveito esse noticiário sobre o Oriente Médio para te contar que um nome bem conhecido da podosfera é o novo colunista da CBN. Ling-2.5-1T is described as a flagship general language model focused on efficient reasoning and agent interaction, capable of handling context lengths up to 1 million tokens while using about 5,890 tokens to reach frontier-like results.
